CCCS ITSG-33 IT Security Risk Management: A Lifecycle Approach

CSE/CCCS ITSG-33 Annex 3A · in force (overview effective 2012-11-01; Annex 3A December 2014 per mapping agent) · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Government of Canada departments' information systems (through the TBS security policy suite) and suppliers whose contracts require ITSG-33 controls; used voluntarily elsewhere.

AU-9 PROTECTION OF AUDIT INFORMATION We detect

db.audit-table-mutableApplication roles or code can update or delete the audit table, so audit information is not protected.

db.cascade-deletes-historyOne ordinary delete erases audit records through ON DELETE CASCADE.

db.audit-table-mutableApplication roles or code can alter or erase audit records, which directly shows the trail lacks the required protection.

db.cascade-deletes-historyRemoving a parent row silently erases its audit records, so the schema itself leaves the trail exposed to deletion.

secrets.insecure-defaultA sample signing secret in the env template or CI config is default authenticator content nothing changes before installation.

secrets.committedCredential material committed to the repository is disclosed to everyone who can read it.

secrets.committedKeys, tokens or env-file secrets sit unencrypted in the application's repository.

secrets.in-historyThe repository history still embeds an unencrypted static authenticator.

SA-4 (1) ACQUISITION PROCESS | FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES OF SECURITY CONTROLSDeveloper must describe the functional properties of the security controls. Coming soon
SA-4 (2) ACQUISITION PROCESS | DESIGN / IMPLEMENTATION INFORMATION FOR SECURITY CONTROLSDeveloper must provide design and implementation details of security controls at a set detail level. Coming soon

SA-4 (5)(b) Keep the secure configurations as defaults for any reinstall or upgrade. Coming soon
SA-4 (6) ACQUISITION PROCESS | USE OF INFORMATION ASSURANCE PRODUCTSCryptographic security products for classified data may need CSE-approved key management and SC-13 compliance.
SA-4 (6)(a) Use only CSE-approved off-the-shelf security products when carrying classified data over lower-level networks. Coming soon
SA-4 (6)(b) Such products must be evaluated or validated by CSE or its procedures. Coming soon
SA-4 (7) ACQUISITION PROCESS | NIAP-APPROVED PROTECTION PROFILESLimit commercial assurance products to evaluated ones, with FIPS-validated cryptography otherwise.
SA-4 (7)(a) Use only commercial security products evaluated against a CSE-approved protection profile when one exists. Coming soon
SA-4 (7)(b) Without a protection profile, cryptographic modules relied upon must be FIPS-validated. Coming soon
SA-4 (8) ACQUISITION PROCESS | CONTINUOUS MONITORING PLANDeveloper must produce a continuous monitoring plan for security control effectiveness. Coming soon
SA-4 (9) ACQUISITION PROCESS | FUNCTIONS / PORTS / PROTOCOLS / SERVICES IN USEDeveloper must identify intended functions, ports, protocols and services early in the lifecycle. Coming soon

SA-11 DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING
SA-11 (A) Developer must create and carry out a security assessment plan. Coming soon
SA-11 (B) Developer must perform chosen testing types at a defined depth and coverage. We detect

coverage.uncoveredThe coverage report shows code no test executes, short of the required test depth and coverage.

tests.no-coverage-floorWithout an enforced threshold, test coverage can fall below any defined coverage unnoticed.
SA-11 (C) Developer must produce evidence of executing the assessment plan and its test results. Coming soon
SA-11 (D) Developer must implement a verifiable flaw remediation process. Coming soon
SA-11 (E) Developer must correct flaws found during security testing. We detect

analyzer.findingAn unsuppressed analyzer error or warning remaining open is a detected flaw left unfixed, which is what this point prohibits.

ci.nonblocking-checksA test or security check that cannot fail the build lets the flaws it finds ship uncorrected.
SA-11 (1) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | STATIC CODE ANALYSISDeveloper must use static code analysis tools for common flaws and document results. Coming soon
SA-11 (2) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | THREAT AND VULNERABILITY ANALYSESDeveloper must perform threat and vulnerability analyses and test the as-built system. We detect

arch.threat-model-missingA network-facing repository with no threat model shows the developer's threat analysis was not performed or not kept.
SA-11 (3) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION OF ASSESSMENT PLANS / EVIDENCEIndependent verification of developer assessment plans and evidence.
SA-11 (3)(a) An independent agent must verify the developer's assessment plan implementation and test evidence. Coming soon
SA-11 (3)(b) Give the independent agent enough information or authority to obtain it. Coming soon
SA-11 (4) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | MANUAL CODE REVIEWSDeveloper must manually review specified code using defined techniques. Coming soon
SA-11 (5) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | PENETRATION TESTING / ANALYSISDeveloper must run penetration testing at defined depth and under defined constraints. Coming soon
SA-11 (6) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | ATTACK SURFACE REVIEWSDeveloper must review the attack surface, covering design and implementation changes and mitigating resulting attack vectors. Coming soon
SA-11 (7) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | VERIFY SCOPE OF TESTING / EVALUATIONDeveloper must verify security testing fully covers the required security controls at a defined depth. Coming soon
SA-11 (8) DEVELOPER SECURITY TESTING AND EVALUATION | DYNAMIC CODE ANALYSISDeveloper must use run-time analysis tools to find common flaws and record the results. Coming soon

SC-8 TRANSMISSION CONFIDENTIALITY AND INTEGRITY We detect

tls.verification-disabledAn on-path party can read or modify traffic once certificate checks are off.
SC-8 (A) Protect confidentiality and/or integrity of information in transit. We detect

tls.verification-disabledSkipping certificate checks permits interception and alteration in transit, directly undermining the required protection of data on the wire.

SI-10 (4) INFORMATION INPUT VALIDATION | REVIEW / TIMING INTERACTIONSAccount for timing interactions between components when deciding responses to invalid inputs. Coming soon
SI-10 (5) INFORMATION INPUT VALIDATION | RESTRICT INPUTS TO TRUSTED SOURCES AND APPROVED FORMATSLimit inputs to defined trusted sources and approved formats, like whitelisting. Coming soon

SI-11 (A) Error messages should help corrective action without exposing information adversaries could exploit. Coming soon
SI-11 (B) Show error messages only to defined personnel or roles. Coming soon

SI-13 PREDICTABLE FAILURE PREVENTION
SI-13 (A) Determine mean time to failure for defined components in their operating environments. Coming soon
SI-13 (B) Provide substitute components and a way to swap active and standby ones at MTTF criteria. Coming soon
SI-13 (1) PREDICTABLE FAILURE PREVENTION | TRANSFERRING COMPONENT RESPONSIBILITIESRetire components by moving duties to substitutes before a set fraction of MTTF. Coming soon
SI-13 (3) PREDICTABLE FAILURE PREVENTION | MANUAL TRANSFER BETWEEN COMPONENTSManually switch between active and standby components at defined intervals when MTTF is exceeded. Coming soon
SI-13 (4) PREDICTABLE FAILURE PREVENTION | STANDBY COMPONENT INSTALLATION / NOTIFICATIONStandby component installation and notification; transfer may be automatic or manual upon failure.
SI-13 (4)(a) On component failure, standby components must be installed transparently within a defined time. Coming soon
SI-13 (4)(b) On component failure, raise an alarm and/or automatically shut the system down. Coming soon

Reuse: Official Government of Canada text, free to read; reuse terms in the site's notice (not re-checked); cite IDs and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.
